name: Do you need a permit to remove a swimming pool in Pasadena or Los Angeles?

mainEntity.name: Is a permit required before pool demolition starts in Pasadena and nearby cities?
mainEntity.text: Is a permit required before pool demolition starts in Pasadena and nearby cities?

acceptedAnswer.text: Permit rules are one of the most common gaps in pool-removal searches because they vary by city and by whether the job is partial or full demolition. In Pasadena, the city requires a building permit before demolition begins, along with a site plan for review. The pool shell must also be removed or modified in a specific way, then backfilled and compacted to a required standard. Other nearby cities may have different permit triggers, inspection steps, and documentation requirements. Homeowners should ask the contractor who is pulling the permit, whether plan review is included, and whether inspections are scheduled as part of the bid. If the property is in a hillside area, near a retaining wall, or has drainage concerns, extra approvals may be needed. Never assume a pool can simply be filled in without paperwork. Permit delays are a common reason projects take longer than expected.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, many Los Angeles-area cities require a permit before pool demolition begins. Pasadena specifically requires a building permit and plan review before work starts, and the project must meet removal, drainage, and compaction requirements. Requirements can vary by city and scope of work.
